text: Select only model_design for a Tier 2 change: add a learned, identity-initialized output projection to the existing NextItNet. The current model uses the same item embeddings for history encoding and target scoring, coupling their two roles in a sparse dataset. This coupling is a plausible representation bottleneck, although the validation HR@10 of 0.665 does not establish its cause. Add one bias-free hidden_units-to-hidden_units linear layer after the final sequence LayerNorm, initialize its weight to the identity, and apply the existing padding mask to its output. This preserves the initial scoring function while allowing training to learn a distinct representation for matching sequence features against candidate embeddings. At width 64, the change introduces only 4,096 parameters and retains one causal dilated-convolution NextItNet without attention, additional prediction branches, or item biases. Return the projected representation from encode_sequence so forward and score_candidates automatically use identical scoring logic while preserving their interfaces and output shapes. Keep all existing convolutional blocks, gates, residual scales, embeddings, hyperparameters, and frozen host behavior unchanged to isolate this experiment. Allocate one candidate slot for the host to compare validation HR@10 against 0.665 using the unchanged split and sampled candidates; claim improvement only from the measured result. Preserve the permitted imports, eight numeric constants, and two classes, with no model-side training, evaluation, printing, file access, or submission generation.
